judge.rationale: All four answers comparably use a shared cytotoxic/NK and myeloid marker core (including GNLY, NKG7, GZMA/GZMB, CD8B, CST3, S100A12, FCN1, LYZ, and CD14) as proxies for cell-state heterogeneity rather than direct PTPRC regulation, but A and D invoke many additional B-cell, erythroid, platelet, HLA, mouse, and ambient-RNA contributors that are absent or only partly represented in B and especially C, so more than half of the complete group-level molecular inventory is not shared and the shared-minority ceiling of 4 applies.
